examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A clique gives a chromatic-number lower bound; a constructed colouring gives an upper bound. Bipartite graphs are exactly those without odd cycles. A nontrivial tree and even cycle need two colours; an odd cycle needs three. A chromatic polynomial counts labelled-colour assignments, allowing colours unused. Triangle-free does not imply bipartite, since longer odd cycles remain possible.

**Key relationship:** χ(Kₙ) = n; χ(C₂ₖ) = 2; χ(C₂ₖ₊₁) = 3 for cycles of length ≥ 3

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Find clique or odd-cycle lower bounds.
2. Construct a matching upper-bound colouring.
3. For counts, decide whether colours are labelled.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For proper vertex colouring, adjacent vertices must differ. Establish a lower bound using a clique or odd cycle, then construct a colouring meeting it. A greedy ordering always uses at most Δ+1 colours but can be suboptimal. Two-colourability is equivalent to bipartiteness and absence of odd cycles, and is tested componentwise by BFS/DFS.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
What is the chromatic number of the cycle C9?

**Answer: 3.** An odd cycle is not bipartite: alternating two colours returns with equal colours on the closing edge. Three suffice: alternate two on the first eight vertices and give the ninth a third colour. Thus the minimum is 3.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An edge crossing in a drawing does not create a graph vertex. A chromatic number k does not imply existence of a k-clique.

Maximum degree is an upper-bound ingredient; it is not generally the chromatic number.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Chromatic number of a 7-cycle?

- **A.** 2
- **B.** 3
- **C.** 7
- **D.** 1

**Answer: B.** Two alternating colours conflict at the closing edge. A third colour at one vertex suffices.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Every tree is bipartite
- **B.** Containing K₄ requires at least four colours
- **C.** Triangle-free implies bipartite
- **D.** An even cycle needs two colours

**Answer: A, B, D.** Trees have no odd cycles, cliques force distinct colours, and even cycles alternate. A 5-cycle refutes C.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

How many proper colourings of a five-vertex tree use a palette of three labelled colours?



**Answer: 48.** The root has 3 choices and each other vertex has 2 choices different from its parent: 3·2⁴=48.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

How many proper colourings of a labelled 5-cycle use a palette of three labelled colours, with unused colours allowed?



**Answer: 30.** For cycle C_n the count with q colours is (q−1)ⁿ+(−1)ⁿ(q−1). Substituting q=3,n=5 gives 32−2=30. Unlike a path, the closing edge imposes an extra constraint.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q60 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/graph-colouring?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Graph colouring. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Label the eight vertices clockwise starting at the upper-left outer vertex. Every drawn edge joins an odd-positioned vertex to an even-positioned vertex, including the long diagonals.
2. Colour odd positions one colour and even positions another; no adjacent vertices share a colour, so two colours suffice.
3. The graph has edges, so one colour is impossible. Its chromatic number is **2**.

#### GATE 2023 CS · Q55 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/graph-colouring?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Graph colouring. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. When a vertex is processed, it avoids every colour used by an already coloured neighbour. Later neighbours must likewise avoid its colour, so the final colouring is proper: A.
2. At most Δ(G) neighbour colours can be forbidden. Among the first Δ(G)+1 colours, at least one is available: B.
3. A clique on Δ+1 vertices disproves C. Greedy colouring can use more colours than optimal depending on vertex order, disproving D. Select **A,B**.
